subject: Integration design & auth options for Jupiter Health
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.inference, marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-09-07T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended auth patterns

Hi Aisha —

Great to meet the Jupiter Health team today. Quick recap and concrete next steps from our discovery: 

What we covered
- Integration targets: real-time triage assistant (chat + structured output), embeddings-based patient note search, and reranking for top-N recommendations.
- Volume profile: bursty peaks (audit days) with steady baseline ~300 reqs/min for inference.
- Security ask: procurement/security will need SOC2 evidence; devs want clear key-rotation guidance.

Recommended initial approach (what we think fits best)
1) Server-to-server traffic (platform <-> Redwood): short-lived service-account tokens minted by a token broker (JWT) + optional KMS-backed signing for on-prem / Private deployments. This gives least blast radius and matches your audit needs.
2) Internal dev/test flows: scoped API keys with strict IP and quota restrictions for low-risk squads. Rotate monthly and automate via CI.
3) Embeddings/ranking: route high-sensitivity data to Dedicated pods + enable prefix caching; use routing policy to fallback to a quantized cheaper model for non-critical queries.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (quickstart), MAP-JupiterHealth.xlsx (mutual action plan).

Next actions
- I’ll share a one-pager with auth tradeoffs and an integration diagram (tomorrow).
- Please loop in your DevOps (devops@jupiterhealth.com) and procurement (procurement@jupiterhealth.com) for SOC2/contract items.
- Can we target a 30-minute technical follow-up next week to walk the SDK quickstart and runbook? Proposed times: Tue/Wed AM PT.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a short POC.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended auth patterns

Hi Aisha —

Thanks — answers inline and attached materials below.

TL;DR: For production we recommend service-account + short-lived JWTs minted by a token broker. API keys are OK for non-production but should be scoped and rotated automatically via CI.

Rotation & token-flow (proposal)- Token broker (customer-run) holds long-lived KMS-protected signing key.
- Issue short-lived JWTs (15m–1h) to services with minimal scopes.
- Renew via standard OAuth client credentials flow (server-to-server) or via our SDK helpers if you run a Redwood Private deployment.
- Rotation cadence: rotate signing key every 90 days; rotate machine credentials monthly.
- Failover: if broker is unavailable we default to a cached short-lived token for a grace period (configurable).

Avoiding embedded keys in services- Use the SDK’s token refresh helper (example in attached auth-options-one-pager.md). That means services never store raw long-lived keys; they hold ephemeral tokens only.

Data handling for embeddings- Client-side PII redaction: recommended to hash patient IDs and strip direct identifiers before sending. We include deterministic hashing helpers in the SDK for common languages. For high-sensitivity workloads, route embeddings requests to Dedicated or Private to keep data on isolated pools.

Structured output & tool calling- For the triage assistant we suggest using structured-output schemas + function/tool calling so you can validate fields before writing back to EHR. We'll share a sample schema in the follow-up demo.

Attachments included: auth-options-one-pager.md, redwood-integration-diagram.png

Proposed next step: 30 min technical review where we walk SDK quickstart, token refresh flow, and the integration diagram. I can do Wed 9/15 9:00–9:30 AM PT or Thu 9/16 11:00–11:30 AM PT.
